binary: .local-state/compact-resident/cirrove-service-compact-release (frozen release, same binary for every arm)
question: Does any glibc allocator configuration bring G3 (released PSS minus indexed_baseline PSS) under the 256 MiB budget on the heavy fixture? Every prior allocator diagnostic used namespace_capacity_baseline, which never exceeds 501 live views.
answer: No. Round 1 lands at 474.3-478.3 MiB in all four runs, a spread of 3.9 MiB, every arm about 1.86x over budget. Allocator configuration is not a route to this gate.
limits: One run per tuned arm, two for the untuned configuration.

The arms ran sequentially through one shared TMPDIR and are therefore confounded with run order; the full arm inherited a directory destroyed and recreated by operator error partway through the series. Only the trim arm had a private untouched TMPDIR, and it has the lowest round-1 value.

Between-run variation in retained RSS is large and already documented: the two untuned runs differ by 6.2 vs 38.4 MiB on the same round step. Absolute G3 beyond round 1 must not be compared across single runs.
No conclusion is drawn here about whether tuning helps or harms. It does not reach the budget, which is the only question this answers.
